newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares gain after delay in oil price hike.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares gain after delay in oil price hike.

text.p: Speculators re-entered the market and pushed up Delhi shares in early trade after India's ruling coalition deferred a decision on whether to raise petroleum product prices, brokers said.
After 30 minutes of trade, the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index was up 4.7 points to 852.34. On Monday the index closed down 1.41 points.
Traders said that operators had sold heavily on Monday on expectations of a petrol price increase.
The ruling United Front coalition on Monday failed to reach a consensus on whether to raise the prices of some petroleum products and deferred a decision until June 27.
"The market is set for another rally," said B.K. Nagpal of stock brokerage B.B. Portfolio.
Reliance Industries climbed 4.85 rupees to 332.50, bolstered by persistent rumours that the company might offer bonus shares at its annual general meeting on June 27.
State Bank of India rose three rupees at 318.50.
Mahanagar Telephone Nigam gained two rupees to 315.
